passage: I'm Vinita from next door, and I've been dropping in on Hafsa most evenings this month. Every evening I watch her son Zayan, nine, redo his homework three or four times because one letter leans. Hafsa sits beside him looking proud and worried at once; she bites her lip, then smiles when he gets it right. Last night he cried over a rubbed-out map. Hafsa didn't say, "Stop being silly." She said, "You care about doing it properly. I love that. But look, yesterday I burnt the rice, and we still ate." He laughed a little. Then she said, "Good enough is fine for homework." I can't tell what he thought, but he closed the book.

qa.q: What does Hafsa's bitten lip suggest while she watches Zayan?
qa.a: It suggests she feels proud and worried at once about how hard he pushes himself.

qa.q: Which of Hafsa's choices helped Zayan most, and why?
qa.a: She praised his care, shared that she had burnt the rice and said good enough is fine, without shaming his high standards.

qa.q: How might Zayan feel hearing that his mother burnt the rice?
qa.a: He may feel relieved and less alone, which is why he laughs a little.

grounding: A neighbour watches a mother torn between pride and worry at her son's perfectionism, who shares her own mistake and says good enough is fine.

passage:
Monday: Uday found Mehak, ten, still at her desk at ten at night, redrawing a science diagram because one arrow was "too thick". He felt a rush of pride at her care, then a knot of worry. "Beta, it's fine," he said. She burst into tears.
Wednesday: He tried something else. At dinner he told her about the document he'd sent at work with a typo on page one. "My boss laughed. I fixed it. The office is still standing." Mehak giggled.
Saturday: While drawing a card for Dadi, Mehak smudged the corner. She froze, then looked at Uday. "Good enough?" she asked. "Good enough," he said. She drew a flower over the smudge.

qa.q: Why was Mehak redrawing the diagram?
What did Uday feel on Monday night, and why?
qa.a: He felt proud of her care but also worried, seeing her still at her desk so late over one arrow.

qa.q: What turning point on Wednesday changed things?
qa.a: Uday shared his own typo at work, showing mistakes can be fixed, which made Mehak giggle and relax.

qa.q: How might Mehak feel asking "Good enough?" on Saturday?
qa.a: She may feel nervous but braver, checking that it's safe to leave a small flaw.

grounding: Over a week, Uday, torn between pride and worry, shares his own mistake, and Mehak begins to accept good enough.
